study type: Secondary analysis of a retrospective cohort study (registry data)
exposure: Maternal temperature less than 39°C (low fever) in the setting of chorioamnionitis
Maternal temperature greater than or equal to 39°C (high fever) in the setting of chorioamnionitis
outcome: Composite of adverse neonatal outcomes (death, sepsis, necrotizing enterocolitis, grade-3 or -4 intraventricular hemorrhage, seizure within 24 hours of delivery, intubation within 24 hours of delivery, requiring cardiopulmonary resuscitation)
cohort: The study included 1,313 women with singleton gestations and chorioamnionitis from the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units (MFMU) Cesarean Registry data (1999-2002).
finding: The degree of maternal fever in the setting of chorioamnionitis was not associated with an increased likelihood of the primary composite adverse neonatal outcomes, even when controlling for confounders or analyzing term infants separately.
